dedupe_keys.name: taiwan disaster case data 災情案件資料 geolocated incident reports with casualties trapped missing and sheltered people during central emergency operation center activations

description: This dataset is Taiwan's live record of individual disaster incidents reported while the Central Emergency Operation Center is activated. It is published by the National Fire Agency of the Ministry of the Interior. Each case has an identifier, time, county, township, place and coordinates, disaster category and subcategory, a description, its handling status and reporting unit, the numbers of people injured, dead, trapped, missing and sheltered, and flags for traffic obstruction and major cases. The current file holds the last seven days of an activation and is refreshed every 20 minutes, and yearly archive datasets for the 2022, 2023 and 2024 activations are listed alongside it. The data are free and available to download as CSV or XML under Taiwan's Open Government Data License. Caveats: the live file covers only the seven days of an activation, so history comes from the yearly archives, texts are in Chinese, and reports reflect what units logged during the emergency. Simulation uses: validating hazard impact and emergency response models against real incident locations and times, estimating the rescue and shelter demand that typhoons create, and mapping road obstructions. Related records: the NCDR public alert feed (data-ncdr-taiwan-cap-public-alerts) carries the warnings issued for the same events, and the San Francisco fire and EMS calls (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) are an example of call-level data.
